category: Studies & solvers II: specialised study steps, sweeps and solver settings
description: Study steps beyond Stationary/Time Dependent/Frequency Domain/Eigenfrequency: modal, boundary-mode and mode analyses, small-signal and prestressed studies, linear buckling, initialization steps, source sweeps, FFT transforms, sensitivity, ray tracing, combine solutions, function/material/batch/cluster sweeps, model reduction, surrogate training and the electrochemistry studies; study-step settings (Physics and Variables Selection, Values of Dependent Variables, load cases, adaptation, results while solving); and the solver-configuration nodes and properties: Parametric continuation, Newton damping and Jacobian update, time-stepping methods and step control, tolerances, eigenvalue search settings, the direct solvers (MUMPS, PARDISO, SPOOLES, dense), iterative solvers (GMRES, FGMRES, BiCGStab, CG) and preconditioners (SOR, ILU, AMG/GMG, domain decomposition), automatic remeshing, time-discrete and modal solvers, optimization solvers, and the solver log/warnings.

tools.name: Frequency Domain, Modal
tools.description: Study that first computes eigenmodes (Eigenfrequency step) and then solves the frequency response by modal superposition in the reduced modal basis, orders of magnitude faster than a full Frequency Domain sweep for structural, acoustic and MEMS models with many frequencies, and allowing modal damping ratios per mode. Accuracy depends on including enough modes (well above the highest frequency of interest) and on the loads being representable by them.
tools.usage: Add Study > Frequency Domain, Modal (adds Eigenfrequency + Frequency Domain, Modal steps); API: model.study("std1").create("eig", "Eigenfrequency"); model.study("std1").create("frmod", "FrequencyDomainModal")

parameters.name: Eigenfrequency step: neigs / shift
parameters.description: Number of modes and search point; include rigid-body modes if free-free.

parameters.name: Frequency Domain, Modal step: plist
parameters.description: Frequency list.

parameters.name: Modal Solver > damping
parameters.description: Modal damping ratios (uniform or per mode) or Rayleigh damping from the physics.

parameters.name: Eigenpairs / Reduced-order model
parameters.description: Option to include the static correction or store the ROM.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS, Acoustics, RF or Wave Optics Module. Time Dependent, Modal is the transient counterpart. Nonlinear or frequency-dependent materials are not supported in the modal basis.

tools.name: Time Dependent, Modal
tools.description: Transient analysis by mode superposition: an Eigenfrequency step supplies the modal basis and the Time Dependent, Modal step integrates the reduced modal equations in time with modal or Rayleigh damping, giving fast transient responses of linear structures/acoustic cavities to impacts, base excitation or shock loads. Not applicable to nonlinear problems or time-varying material properties.
tools.usage: Add Study > Time Dependent, Modal; API: model.study("std1").create("eig", "Eigenfrequency"); model.study("std1").create("tdmod", "TimeDependentModal")

parameters.name: tlist
parameters.description: Output times.

parameters.name: Modal damping
parameters.description: Damping ratios per mode or from the physics damping nodes.

parameters.name: Number of modes
parameters.description: From the Eigenfrequency step; must span the excitation bandwidth.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS, Acoustics, RF or Wave Optics Module. Loads are projected on the modal basis at each time step; high-frequency content beyond the modes is lost.

tools.name: Boundary Mode Analysis
tools.description: Study step that solves an eigenvalue problem on a port boundary (2D cross-section of a waveguide, optical fibre, transmission line, acoustic duct, or a Solid Mechanics cross-section) to find the propagating modes and their propagation constants (effective mode index), which the Numeric Port then uses as its mode field in the subsequent Frequency Domain (or Wavelength Domain / Beam Envelopes) step. One Boundary Mode Analysis step is added per numeric port, each with the port name and the mode search settings.
tools.usage: Add Study > Boundary Mode Analysis (combined with Frequency Domain); API: model.study("std1").create("bma", "BoundaryModeAnalysis"); bma.set("PortName", "1"); set("modeFreq", "f0"); set("neigs", 1); set("shift", "1.45")

parameters.name: PortName
parameters.description: Port whose modes are computed.

parameters.name: modeFreq / wavelength
parameters.description: Frequency at which the mode is computed (usually the same as the sweep or a parameter).

parameters.name: neigs / shift (search for modes around)
parameters.description: Number of modes and the effective index/propagation constant to search near.

parameters.name: Transform
parameters.description: Effective mode index | Propagation constant | Out-of-plane wave number.

tools.notes: Requires the RF, Wave Optics, Acoustics or Structural Mechanics Module. For frequency sweeps the mode must be recomputed at each frequency: put the Boundary Mode Analysis and Frequency Domain steps inside a Parametric Sweep over the frequency parameter. Mode Analysis is the stand-alone 2D version without a port.

tools.name: Mode Analysis
tools.description: 2D (or 2D axisymmetric) eigenvalue study computing the propagating modes of a waveguide cross-section for the Electromagnetic Waves and Pressure Acoustics interfaces: effective mode index/propagation constant, mode field, dispersion (with a parametric sweep over frequency/wavelength), cut-off frequencies and characteristic impedance. Used for fibre and integrated-optics design, microwave transmission lines and acoustic ducts.
tools.usage: Add Study > Mode Analysis (2D components); API: model.study("std1").create("mode", "ModeAnalysis"); set("modeFreq", "f0"); set("neigs", 6); set("shift", "1.45")

parameters.name: modeFreq
parameters.description: Mode analysis frequency (or wavelength).

parameters.name: neigs / shift
parameters.description: Number of modes and the effective index (or wave number) to search around.

parameters.name: Transform
parameters.description: Effective mode index | Propagation constant | Out-of-plane wave number | Cutoff frequency.

tools.notes: Requires the RF, Wave Optics or Acoustics Module. Use a PML or scattering boundary around leaky structures; the imaginary part of neff gives the loss.

tools.name: Small-Signal Analysis, Frequency Domain (Frequency-Domain Perturbation)
tools.description: Two-step study computing a stationary (possibly nonlinear) bias/operating point and then the linearised harmonic response to small perturbations about it - the Frequency-Domain Perturbation step uses linper() loads and the linearization point from the first step. Standard for semiconductor AC analysis, MEMS with DC bias plus AC drive, nonlinear magnetic devices with small ripple, and electrochemical impedance (AC Impedance studies are the same idea).
tools.usage: Add Study > Small-Signal Analysis, Frequency Domain (Stationary + Frequency-Domain Perturbation); loads marked with linper(); API: model.study("std1").create("stat", "Stationary"); model.study("std1").create("frlin", "Frequencylinearized") (type name as generated by the GUI: save as Java to confirm)

parameters.name: Linearization point
parameters.description: Solution of the preceding stationary step (set automatically).

parameters.name: plist
parameters.description: Perturbation frequencies.

parameters.name: linper(expr)
parameters.description: Operator marking the harmonic-perturbation part of a load; lindev()/lintotal() evaluate results.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC, MEMS or Semiconductor Module (perturbation solver is in the core product for some interfaces). Perturbation quantities are complex; use lindev() to extract the harmonic part and linpoint() for the bias.

tools.name: Eigenfrequency, Prestressed / Frequency Domain, Prestressed
tools.description: Two-step studies where a Stationary step (with geometric nonlinearity) computes a preload state - centrifugal stiffening of a rotating blade, tension in a string or membrane, thermal stress, pressure in a vessel, MEMS bias - and the Eigenfrequency or Frequency Domain step then linearises around it, so stress stiffening and softening change the natural frequencies and responses. Frequency Domain, Prestressed, Modal adds mode superposition.
tools.usage: Add Study > Eigenfrequency, Prestressed / Frequency Domain, Prestressed; API: model.study("std1").create("stat", "Stationary"); stat.set("geometricNonlinearity", true); model.study("std1").create("eig", "Eigenfrequency"); eig.set("geometricNonlinearity", true); eig.set("usesol", "on"); eig.set("initstudy", "std1")... (the wizard sets the linearization point automatically)

parameters.name: Stationary step
parameters.description: Preload with Include geometric nonlinearity.

parameters.name: Eigenfrequency/Frequency Domain step
parameters.description: Values of Dependent Variables > Linearization point: from the stationary solution.

parameters.name: Prestress option in physics
parameters.description: Alternatively, Initial Stress and Strain gives a known prestress without the first step.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics, MEMS, Geomechanics or Acoustics Module. Linear Buckling is the related study that finds the load factor at which the prestressed stiffness becomes singular.

tools.name: Linear Buckling
tools.description: Two-step study (Stationary + Linear Buckling) that solves the eigenvalue problem (K + lambda*K_G) phi = 0 with the geometric stiffness K_G from a unit reference load, returning the critical load factor lambda (the reference load times lambda is the buckling load) and the buckling mode shapes. Used for columns, shells, plates and frames; the mode can be used as an imperfection for a subsequent nonlinear post-buckling analysis.
tools.usage: Add Study > Linear Buckling; API: model.study("std1").create("stat", "Stationary"); model.study("std1").create("buckling", "LinearBuckling"); buckling.set("neigs", 4)

parameters.name: neigs
parameters.description: Number of buckling modes (lowest critical load factors).

parameters.name: shift
parameters.description: Load factor to search around (default 1).

parameters.name: Reference load
parameters.description: The loads applied in the Stationary step; results give solid.lambda (critical load factor).

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module. Negative load factors mean buckling under reversed load; imperfection-sensitive shells need a nonlinear (Stationary with continuation) analysis for the real collapse load.

tools.name: Stationary / Time Dependent with Initialization
tools.description: Preset studies for turbulent flow (and some discharge/plasma models) that add an initialization step - Wall Distance Initialization for the reciprocal wall distance needed by low-Re turbulence models, or Electrostatics Initialization - before the Stationary or Time Dependent step, with the Physics and Variables Selection set so each step solves only its own variables. Adding the turbulent-flow interface through the Model Wizard chooses these automatically.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies > Stationary with Initialization / Time Dependent with Initialization; API: model.study("std1").create("wdi", "WallDistanceInitialization"); model.study("std1").create("stat", "Stationary")

parameters.name: Initialization step
parameters.description: Solves the wd interface only.

parameters.name: Main step
parameters.description: Uses the initialization solution for the variables not solved for.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (turbulence) or Heat Transfer Module for the nonisothermal variants. If the geometry or mesh changes, the wall distance must be recomputed - keep both steps in the same study.

tools.name: Wall Distance Initialization
tools.description: Study step that solves the Wall Distance interface (reciprocal wall distance G) once, before the flow, for turbulence models that need the distance to the nearest wall (SST, Spalart-Allmaras, k-omega low-Re, v2-f, LES/DES wall models). It is stationary and cheap, and its solution is stored so subsequent steps reuse it.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Other > Wall Distance Initialization; API: model.study("std1").create("wdi", "WallDistanceInitialization")

parameters.name: Physics and Variables Selection
parameters.description: Only the wd (or spf.wd) contribution is solved.

parameters.name: Mesh selection
parameters.description: Must be the same mesh as the flow step.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Parametric sweeps over geometry parameters must include this step inside the sweep.

tools.name: Stationary Source Sweep / Frequency Domain Source Sweep
tools.description: Study steps that automatically excite each source (terminal, coil, port, lumped port) in turn with the others passive and assemble the full lumped matrix from the results: Stationary Source Sweep gives capacitance (Electrostatics), inductance/resistance (Magnetic Fields, Currents Only, mf) matrices, and Frequency Domain Source Sweep gives the S-parameter (or admittance/impedance) matrix in RF/AC-DC frequency-domain models, reusing the LU factorisation across sources for speed. Variants 'with Initialization' add the coil geometry/current analysis first.
tools.usage: Add Study > Stationary Source Sweep / Frequency Domain Source Sweep; API: model.study("std1").create("ssw", "StationarySourceSweep"); model.study("std1").create("fdsw", "FrequencyDomainSourceSweep") (confirm type names from a saved Java file)

parameters.name: Sources
parameters.description: Automatically detected terminals/ports; the sweep index variable enumerates them.

parameters.name: plist (frequency sweep)
parameters.description: Frequencies for the source sweep.

parameters.name: Results
parameters.description: es.C11.. / mfco.L11.. / emw.S11.. matrix variables and the Global Matrix Evaluation / Touchstone export.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module (stationary) or RF/Wave Optics/AC-DC Module (frequency). Terminal Sweep settings in the interface are the older manual equivalent.

tools.name: Time to Frequency FFT / Frequency to Time FFT
tools.description: Study steps that transform a stored time-dependent solution into the frequency domain by FFT (spectra of transient acoustics, EM pulse responses, S-parameters from time-domain simulations, vibration signals) or a frequency-domain solution into the time domain (impulse responses from a frequency sweep, Time Dependent with FFT presets in rotordynamics). Settings control the input solution, time/frequency ranges, windowing and the output scaling.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Frequency Domain > Time to Frequency FFT; Study > Study Steps > Time Dependent > Frequency to Time FFT; API: model.study("std2").create("tffft", "TimeToFreqFFT") (check the generated type name); set("tlist"/"plist", ...)

parameters.name: Input study / solution
parameters.description: The time-dependent (or frequency-domain) solution to transform.

parameters.name: Input time range / sampling
parameters.description: Start and end time, time step (interpolated) - determines frequency resolution and maximum frequency.

parameters.name: Output frequencies / scaling
parameters.description: Frequency list and scaling (discrete or continuous FFT), windowing function (6.x).

tools.notes: Core product feature. The transform is applied to all DOFs, producing a full frequency-domain dataset (large); for a single probe signal it is cheaper to export the table and use an FFT in MATLAB/Python.

tools.name: Sensitivity (study step)
tools.description: Study step attached to a Stationary, Time Dependent or Frequency Domain solve that computes derivatives of one or more objective functionals with respect to sensitivity/control variables or global parameters (Parameters as sensitivity variables in 6.x) by the adjoint or forward method, exposing them as fsens(var) variables. It is the building block of the Optimization solver and a cheap way to rank design parameters.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Other > Sensitivity (or the Sensitivity section of a Stationary step in 6.x); API: model.study("std1").create("sens", "Sensitivity"); or stat.set("sensitivity", true); stat.set("sensmethod", "adjoint")

parameters.name: Objective function
parameters.description: Expression(s) or references to Optimization/Sensitivity interface objectives.

parameters.name: Control/sensitivity variables
parameters.description: Global parameters or control variables with respect to which derivatives are computed.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Adjoint (one solve per objective) or Forward (one solve per variable).

tools.notes: Core product feature. Objectives must be differentiable with respect to the solution; geometry parameters require the Optimization Module's shape features.

tools.name: Coil Geometry Analysis
tools.description: AC/DC Module study step that precomputes the current-flow direction field of Coil features with 'Numeric' coil type (arbitrary 3D winding shapes with input/output boundaries) by solving an auxiliary problem, before the Magnetic Fields study uses it as a source. Required for all numeric coils; automatically inserted by the Model Wizard as 'Coil Geometry Analysis' preceding Stationary or Frequency Domain.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Other > Coil Geometry Analysis; API: model.study("std1").create("ccc", "CoilCurrentCalculation")

parameters.name: Coil features
parameters.description: All numeric coils in the selected physics are analysed.

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: Solver tolerance for the direction field (default fine).

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. Each coil needs Input and Output boundary subnodes (or a Symmetry Specification) so that the analysis has a well-posed flow problem.

tools.name: Ray Tracing / Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing
tools.description: Studies for the Geometrical Optics and Ray Acoustics interfaces: Ray Tracing integrates the ray equations over a time (or optical path length) list, and Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing iterates between a Ray Tracing step and a Stationary step for the coupled fields (temperature via Ray Heating, or structural deformation via stress-optical effects), repeating for a given number of iterations until the ray-field solution is self-consistent. Time-dependent Ray Tracing is the only way rays are computed; 'time' can be replaced by optical path length as the parameter.
tools.usage: Add Study > Ray Tracing / Bidirectionally Coupled Ray Tracing; API: model.study("std1").create("rtra", "RayTracing"); rtra.set("tlist", "range(0,1e-10,2e-9)"); model.study("std1").create("bcrt", "BidirectionallyCoupledRayTracing")

parameters.name: tlist / Time step specification
parameters.description: Output times or optical path lengths; 'Strict' stepping ensures rays stop at boundaries.

parameters.name: Number of iterations (bidirectional)
parameters.description: Ray-field coupling iterations.

parameters.name: Stop condition
parameters.description: Stop when all rays are frozen/absorbed.

tools.notes: Requires the Ray Optics Module or Acoustics Module (Ray Acoustics). Bidirectionally Coupled Particle Tracing is the analogous study for space-charge-limited charged-particle beams.

tools.name: Combine Solutions
tools.description: Study step that merges two solutions (or solution sets) into one dataset: concatenate parametric solutions from different runs, sum/subtract solutions (e.g. total minus background field, difference between two designs), or remove selected solutions from a parametric set. The combined solution behaves like any other for postprocessing.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Other > Combine Solutions; API: model.study("std2").create("comsol", "CombineSolutions"); set("combineMethod", "concatenate"|"sum"|"difference"|"remove")

parameters.name: Combination method
parameters.description: Concatenate | Sum | Difference | Remove.

parameters.name: First / Second solution
parameters.description: Study and solution references, with parameter selection.

parameters.name: Solution operation scaling
parameters.description: Weights for sums/differences.

tools.notes: Core product feature (5.4+). The Join dataset in Results is the postprocessing-only alternative for differences; Combine Solutions creates a real solution object usable as initial values.

tools.name: Function Sweep / Material Sweep
tools.description: Study extension steps (like Parametric Sweep) that sweep over the cases of a Function Switch (alternative function definitions) or a Material Switch (alternative materials assigned to the same domains), solving the study for each case and storing the results as an outer parametric solution, so designs with several candidate materials or load profiles are compared in one run and one plot.
tools.usage: Study > Study Extensions > Function Sweep / Material Sweep; API: model.study("std1").create("fsweep", "FunctionSweep"); model.study("std1").create("msweep", "MaterialSweep"); set("sweeptype", "sweepall"|"cases")

parameters.name: Switch
parameters.description: The Function Switch / Material Switch node to sweep.

parameters.name: Cases
parameters.description: All cases or a selected list of case indices.

parameters.name: Sweep type
parameters.description: All combinations or specified combinations when several switches exist.

tools.notes: Core product features (5.2+). Results are indexed by the switch case as an outer solution; use Global plots with 'x-axis data: case number' or Parameterized names.

tools.name: Batch Sweep / Cluster Sweep
tools.description: Parametric sweeps executed as independent batch jobs: Batch Sweep launches separate COMSOL batch processes on the local machine (or a remote machine) for the parameter values, running several in parallel and synchronising the results back to the model (with Job Configurations > Batch nodes), while Cluster Sweep submits them to a cluster scheduler (SLURM, PBS, LSF, Windows HPC, or SSH) as distributed jobs. Both isolate parameter cases so a failure does not stop the others and long sweeps survive GUI closure.
tools.usage: Study > Study Extensions > Batch Sweep / Cluster Sweep; Job Configurations > Batch / Cluster Computing settings; API: model.study("std1").create("bsweep", "BatchSweep"); model.study("std1").create("csweep", "ClusterSweep"); model.batch().create(...)

parameters.name: pname / plistarr / punit
parameters.description: Parameters and value lists, as in Parametric Sweep.

parameters.name: Number of simultaneous jobs / cores per job
parameters.description: Parallelism on the local machine or cluster.

parameters.name: Batch settings
parameters.description: Batch directory, filename, synchronize solutions/accumulated probe table, external COMSOL installation.

parameters.name: Cluster settings
parameters.description: Scheduler type, number of nodes, host file, queue, prepend/postpend commands.

tools.notes: Core product features (Cluster Sweep needs a Floating Network Licence for distributed jobs). The 'Batch' and 'Cluster Computing' entries in the first studies chunk cover the Job Configuration nodes; comsol batch -job runs a configured job from the command line.

tools.name: Study Reference
tools.description: Study step that runs another study as part of the current study sequence, so a chain of studies (e.g. geometry/mesh initialisation, a steady flow, then a transient species transport) can be executed with one Compute and used inside sweeps or optimisation loops. The referenced study keeps its own solver configuration.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Other > Study Reference; API: model.study("std2").create("stdref", "StudyReference"); set("studyref", "std1")

parameters.name: studyref
parameters.description: Tag of the study to run.

tools.notes: Core product feature (5.3+). Combine with Parametric Sweep in the outer study to sweep a whole multi-study workflow.

tools.name: Model Reduction / Modal Reduced-Order Model
tools.description: Study steps that build a reduced-order model (ROM) from a full model: Model Reduction uses modal (eigenmode) or Krylov/AWE bases with training studies for time-dependent and frequency-domain linear systems and creates a Reduced-Order Model node under Global Definitions whose state-space matrices can be exported (to MATLAB/Simulink via LiveLink or as files) or evaluated inside apps; the Modal Reduced-Order Model and Frequency Domain, AWE ROM presets set this up for structural/acoustic/EM wave problems. Compact models for control design and digital twins come from here.
tools.usage: Add Study > Model Reduction (with the training Eigenfrequency/Frequency Domain/Time Dependent study); Global Definitions > Reduced-Order Modeling > Reduced-Order Model; API: model.study("std2").create("mr", "ModelReduction"); model.reduced()...

parameters.name: Training study / Unreduced model study
parameters.description: Studies supplying the basis (modes) and the full system.

parameters.name: Reduced-order model inputs / outputs
parameters.description: Global inputs (parameters, loads) and outputs (probes, global expressions).

parameters.name: Reduction method
parameters.description: Modal (eigenmodes) | AWE (asymptotic waveform evaluation) | Krylov; number of modes/order.

tools.notes: Core product feature (5.6+ for the general Model Reduction study; modal ROMs need the modal solvers' modules). mphreduction in LiveLink for MATLAB extracts the same matrices for use in MATLAB.

tools.name: Surrogate Model Training / Uncertainty Quantification
tools.description: Uncertainty Quantification Module studies: Uncertainty Quantification performs screening (Morris), sensitivity analysis (Sobol indices), uncertainty propagation (PDFs of outputs) and reliability analysis (probability of failure, inverse UQ) by sampling input parameters with given distributions and fitting surrogate models (Gaussian process, PCE, DNN) adaptively; Surrogate Model Training (6.2+) generates a design of experiments over parameters, runs the model for each sample and writes a table that a Gaussian Process / DNN / PCE function is trained on, for use in apps and optimisation.
tools.usage: Add Study > Uncertainty Quantification / Surrogate Model Training; API: model.study("std2").create("uq", "UncertaintyQuantification"); model.study("std2").create("smt", "SurrogateModelTraining")

parameters.name: Quantities of interest
parameters.description: Global scalar expressions/probes evaluated per sample.

parameters.name: Input parameters and distributions
parameters.description: Uniform, normal, lognormal, Weibull... or a parameter range for DOE.

parameters.name: UQ type
parameters.description: Screening | Sensitivity analysis | Uncertainty propagation | Reliability analysis | Inverse UQ.

parameters.name: Sampling / surrogate settings
parameters.description: Number of samples, Latin hypercube/Sobol sequence, surrogate type and error tolerance.

tools.notes: Requires the Uncertainty Quantification Module (6.1+). Results appear as tables and dedicated plots (Sobol Index, Joint Probability Distribution, Kernel Density Estimation datasets).

tools.name: AC Impedance / Cyclic Voltammetry (electrochemistry studies)
tools.description: Preset studies of the electrochemistry modules: AC Impedance, Initial Values / Stationary / Time Dependent add a frequency-domain perturbation step around an equilibrium, a stationary polarisation point or a transient state to compute electrochemical impedance spectra (Nyquist and Bode plots of cell impedance), and Cyclic Voltammetry sets up a time-dependent study with a triangular potential sweep (start/vertex potentials, scan rate, number of cycles) producing current-voltage voltammograms. Both configure the solver for the small-signal or fast-transient character of the problem.
tools.usage: Add Study > AC Impedance, Stationary / Cyclic Voltammetry (electrochemistry interfaces present); API: model.study("std1").create("cv", "CyclicVoltammetry"); cv.set("vstart", ...); model.study("std2").create("stat", "Stationary"); model.study("std2").create("frlin", "FrequencyDomainPerturbation") (check generated names)

parameters.name: Cyclic Voltammetry: Vstart, Vvertex1, Vvertex2, scan rate, cycles
parameters.description: Potential waveform and number of cycles.

parameters.name: AC Impedance: frequency list, perturbation amplitude
parameters.description: Frequencies (log spaced) and the linper() amplitude applied at the electrode.

parameters.name: Results
parameters.description: Impedance Nyquist/Bode plots (real/imag of the cell impedance variable), voltammogram Global plots.

tools.notes: Requires the Electrochemistry, Battery Design, Corrosion, Electrodeposition or Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module. The Electrode Surface / Electrode Current features expose an 'AC perturbation' option used by the impedance studies.

tools.name: Physics and Variables Selection (study step section)
tools.description: Section of every study step listing the physics interfaces and multiphysics couplings in the model with a Solve for check box and a Discretization choice, so a step can solve only a subset (e.g. flow first, heat second in a one-way coupled model, or exclude a Fatigue interface from the structural solve) and can pick a different discretization (physics-controlled or an alternative shape order). Modify model configuration for study step additionally lets you disable individual features (loads, materials) per step, which is how load cases and staged construction are set up.
tools.usage: Study step settings > Physics and Variables Selection: Solve for check boxes; Modify model configuration for study step > disable features; API: model.study("std1").feature("stat").setSolveFor("/physics/ht", false); model.study("std1").feature("stat").set("disabledphysics", ...) / activate("ht", false)

parameters.name: activate / setSolveFor
parameters.description: Per-physics on/off for solving in this step.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Physics settings or an alternative discretization defined in the interface.

parameters.name: Modify model configuration
parameters.description: Disable features (physics nodes, multiphysics couplings, materials) for this step only.

tools.notes: Variables not solved for take their values from the settings in Values of Dependent Variables (by default the previous step's solution), which is what makes sequential one-way coupling work.

tools.name: Values of Dependent Variables (study step section)
tools.description: Study-step section controlling where the initial values of the variables solved for and the values of variables not solved for come from: Physics-controlled (Initial Values nodes), or a User controlled choice of another study/solution (with parameter or time selection), which is how a study is restarted from a previous solution, a transient starts from a converged stationary state, a prestressed analysis references its bias solution, or a one-way coupled step reads the fields of the preceding step. Also holds the Linearization point selection for perturbation/eigenfrequency steps.
tools.usage: Study step settings > Values of Dependent Variables > Initial values of variables solved for / Values of variables not solved for: Solution: std1/sol1 (Automatic, or a specific time/parameter); API: model.study("std2").feature("time").set("useinitsol", "on"); set("initmethod", "sol"); set("initstudy", "std1"); set("solnum", "last"); set("usesol", "on"); set("notsolmethod", "sol"); set("notstudy", "std1")

parameters.name: useinitsol / initmethod / initstudy / solnum
parameters.description: Initial values from a solution: on, method (init | sol), study tag, solution number (first | last | index).

parameters.name: usesol / notsolmethod / notstudy / notsolnum
parameters.description: Values of variables not solved for from a solution.

parameters.name: Linearization point
parameters.description: For Eigenfrequency/Frequency-Domain Perturbation steps: Zero solution or a stored solution.

tools.notes: In the generated solver sequence these settings appear in the Dependent Variables node (initial value and 'values of variables not solved for' settings). A referenced solution must exist on the same mesh or be mapped (COMSOL interpolates automatically when the mesh differs).

tools.name: Load Cases (Define load cases)
tools.description: Stationary study-step section (Study Extensions > Define load cases) that solves a linear or nonlinear problem for several combinations of Load Groups and Constraint Groups (defined under Global Definitions) with scale factors, producing one solution per load case that can be superposed or evaluated separately. It replaces repeated solves for structural load combinations (dead + live + wind), thermal-mechanical scenarios and multi-electrode excitation, and is the input for Fatigue's cumulative damage.
tools.usage: Global Definitions > Load and Constraint Groups > Load Group; assign loads to groups in their settings; Study > Stationary > Study Extensions > Define load cases table; API: model.study("std1").feature("stat").set("useloadcase", "on"); set("loadcase", ...)

parameters.name: Load groups / Constraint groups
parameters.description: Global Definitions nodes (lg1, cg1) that loads/constraints belong to.

parameters.name: Load case table
parameters.description: Name, weight (scale factor) per load group, on/off per constraint group.

parameters.name: Results
parameters.description: Solutions indexed by load case name; Load Case Combination in Results (6.x) for linear superposition.

tools.notes: Core product feature. For linear problems the solver reuses the factorisation so many load cases are almost free; nonlinear problems are solved one by one.

tools.name: Adaptation and Error Estimates (adaptive mesh refinement)
tools.description: Section of the Stationary, Eigenvalue/Eigenfrequency and Time Dependent study steps that turns on adaptive mesh refinement: after each solve an error indicator (L2-norm residual based, or a user expression such as a gradient) is evaluated element-wise and the mesh is refined (longest-edge, regular, or complete remesh with new sizes) where the indicator is largest, for a given number of adaptations or until the error estimate falls below a tolerance. In time-dependent studies the mesh is re-adapted at intervals (time-adaptive), typically for moving fronts and interfaces.
tools.usage: Study > Stationary > Adaptation and Error Estimates > Adaptation and error estimates: Adaptation and error estimates / Error estimates only; API: model.study("std1").feature("stat").set("adaption", "on"); set("adaptmesh", "mesh1"); set("maxadapt", 3); set("errorest", "l2")

parameters.name: Adaptation method
parameters.description: General modification (remesh with size expression) | Longest edge refinement | Regular refinement | Rebuild mesh.

parameters.name: Error indicator
parameters.description: L2 norm residual based (default) or user-defined expression (e.g. abs(ht.gradT)).

parameters.name: Maximum number of adaptations / element growth
parameters.description: Iterations and how many elements may be added per step.

parameters.name: Time-adaptive settings
parameters.description: Adaptation interval (time steps) and mesh coarsening.

tools.notes: Core product feature. The 'Adapt' entry in the Mesh chunk covers the Mesh > Adapt operation used for manual adaptation. Adaptive refinement in the frequency domain is available for RF (Frequency Domain, RF Adaptive Mesh).

tools.name: Results While Solving
tools.description: Study-step section that updates a chosen plot group (and probe plots) in the Graphics window at each solver iteration, time step or parameter value while the study runs, so convergence problems, oscillations or geometry motion can be seen immediately and the run stopped early. Combined with probes it is the standard monitoring setup for long transient and turbulent flow runs.
tools.usage: Study step > Results While Solving > Plot: check box and Plot group; Update at: Time steps / Parameter values / Iterations; API: model.study("std1").feature("time").set("plot", "on"); set("plotgroup", "pg1"); set("plotfreq", "tout")

parameters.name: plot / plotgroup
parameters.description: Enable and choose the plot group.

parameters.name: plotfreq
parameters.description: tout (output times) | tsteps (every solver step) | manual interval.

parameters.name: Probes
parameters.description: All | None | Manual list of probes to plot during solving.

tools.notes: Plotting each step slows the solve slightly; in batch mode it is ignored unless -createplots/-graphics are used. Probe tables accumulate regardless.

tools.name: Parametric (continuation solver node)
tools.description: Attribute node of the Stationary Solver (API type Parametric) created when a study has an Auxiliary sweep or Continuation: it steps through parameter values, using the previous solution (with linear or constant predictor) as the initial guess for the next, and with 'Continuation' can adaptively refine the parameter step when Newton fails - the way to solve strongly nonlinear problems by ramping loads, voltages or material nonlinearity, and to trace load-displacement curves (with the 'Sweep type' and step-size control). Nested parameters produce combined or 'all combinations' sweeps.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Stationary Solver 1 > Parametric 1 (p1); API: model.sol("sol1").feature("s1").create("p1", "Parametric"); p1.set("pname", new String[]{"F"}); p1.set("plistarr", new String[]{"range(0,100,1000)"}); p1.set("pcontinuationmode", "auto")

parameters.name: pname / plistarr / punit
parameters.description: Parameter names, value lists and units.

parameters.name: pcontinuationmode
parameters.description: no | auto | manual - continuation with automatic step adaptation.

parameters.name: porder
parameters.description: constant | linear predictor for the initial guess.

parameters.name: preusesol
parameters.description: auto | yes | no - reuse the previous solution as initial value.

parameters.name: pstep / pminstep / pmaxstep (manual)
parameters.description: Initial, minimum and maximum parameter step for continuation.

tools.notes: The study step's Auxiliary sweep section writes these settings; editing them directly in the solver requires the solver sequence not to be regenerated. Parametric Sweep (study extension) instead solves independent problems and is the choice when parameters change geometry or mesh.

tools.name: Newton damping and Jacobian update (Fully Coupled / Segregated settings)
tools.description: Method and Termination settings of the Fully Coupled and Segregated Step attribute nodes that control the damped Newton iteration: Nonlinear method Constant (Newton) with a fixed damping factor, Automatic (Newton) with adaptive damping, Automatic highly nonlinear (Newton) for stiff problems, Double dogleg (trust region), or a Pseudo time stepping option for stationary flow; Jacobian update On every iteration / Minimal / Once; Termination technique by tolerance or by iterations, with maximum iterations and tolerance factor. These are the first knobs to turn when a stationary solve does not converge.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Stationary Solver > Fully Coupled 1 > Method and Termination; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("s1").feature("fc1").set("dtech", "auto"|"const"|"hnlin"|"ddog"); set("jtech", "onevery"|"minimal"|"once"); set("maxiter", 50); set("ntolfact", 1); set("damp", 0.9); set("minstep", 1e-6)

parameters.name: dtech
parameters.description: const | auto | hnlin | ddog | ptc (pseudo time stepping) - damping technique.

parameters.name: damp / minstep / maxstep
parameters.description: Constant damping factor, and limits for the automatic damping.

parameters.name: jtech
parameters.description: onevery | minimal | once - Jacobian update frequency.

parameters.name: maxiter / ntolfact / termonres
parameters.description: Maximum Newton iterations, tolerance factor relative to the study tolerance, residual-based termination.

tools.notes: Automatic highly nonlinear with many iterations plus a Parametric continuation of the load usually rescues convergence; a small constant damping (0.1-0.3) is a last resort. The 'Fully Coupled' and 'Segregated' entries in the first solver chunk describe the nodes themselves.

tools.name: Time stepping methods (BDF / Generalized alpha / Runge-Kutta)
tools.description: Time-Dependent Solver setting selecting the integrator: BDF (implicit backward differentiation, variable order 1-5, robust and damped - default for most problems), Generalized alpha (second-order, controllable numerical damping, preferred for structural dynamics, acoustics and wave problems where BDF damps too much), explicit Runge-Kutta families (RK34, Dormand-Prince 5, Cash-Karp 5) and Adams-Bashforth for non-stiff ODE systems and time-explicit dG interfaces. Companion settings: maximum/minimum BDF order, initial step, and the amplification factor for high frequencies (rho_inf) of generalized alpha.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Time-Dependent Solver > Time Stepping > Method; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("t1").set("timemethod", "bdf"|"genalpha"|"rungekutta"|"dopri5"|"cashkarp5"|"adamsbashforth3"); set("maxorder", 2); set("rhoinf", 0.75)

parameters.name: timemethod
parameters.description: bdf | genalpha | rungekutta (RK34) | dopri5 | cashkarp5 | adamsbashforth3 | ...

parameters.name: maxorder / minorder
parameters.description: BDF order limits (max 2 recommended for wave-like problems).

parameters.name: rhoinf
parameters.description: Generalized alpha high-frequency amplification factor (0 = maximum damping, 1 = none).

parameters.name: initialstepbdfactive / initialstepbdf
parameters.description: Manual initial time step.

tools.notes: Physics interfaces set a suitable default through 'Transient solver' hints (e.g. Solid Mechanics requests generalized alpha). BDF at order 1 is very dissipative: check that maxorder is not 1 when accuracy matters.

tools.name: Steps taken by solver (Free / Strict / Intermediate / Manual)
tools.description: Time-Dependent Solver setting deciding how the internal time steps relate to the output times in the study's time list: Free lets the error estimator choose steps and interpolates output (default, fastest), Strict forces the solver to hit every output time and never step beyond it (needed when inputs change abruptly at listed times, for pulses and events, and for consistent FFT sampling), Intermediate takes at least one step between outputs, and Manual uses a fixed step (with 'Time step' expression) for explicit control and when comparing with other codes. Maximum step constraints and the initial step complete the step control.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Time-Dependent Solver > Time Stepping > Steps taken by solver; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("t1").set("tstepsbdf", "free"|"strict"|"intermediate"|"manual"); set("maxstepconstraintbdf", "const"); set("maxstepbdf", "1e-4"); set("timestepbdf", "1e-5") (property names end in genalpha for generalized alpha)

parameters.name: tstepsbdf / tstepsgenalpha
parameters.description: free | strict | intermediate | manual.

parameters.name: maxstepconstraintbdf / maxstepbdf
parameters.description: Maximum step: none | const | expr and its value.

parameters.name: timestepbdf
parameters.description: Fixed step for manual mode.

parameters.name: initialstepbdfactive / initialstepbdf
parameters.description: Initial step control.

tools.notes: Free stepping can jump over short events entirely; when a source is a narrow pulse use Strict or a maximum step. The study step's tlist defines output times only, not the accuracy - that is governed by the tolerances.

tools.name: Tolerances (relative and absolute)
tools.description: Error control of the Time-Dependent Solver and study step: the relative tolerance (study step, default 0.01 or 0.001 depending on physics) and the absolute tolerance (Time-Dependent Solver node: global scaled/unscaled value, or per-variable factors) together define the accepted local error per step (err_i <= rtol*|u_i| + atol_i), driving the automatic step-size and order selection; the Stationary and Fully Coupled nodes use the relative tolerance with a tolerance factor for Newton termination. Tightening rtol is the first check when transient results look step-dependent.
tools.usage: Study > Time Dependent > Relative tolerance; Solver Configurations > Time-Dependent Solver > Absolute Tolerance; API: model.study("std1").feature("time").set("rtol", 1e-4); model.sol("sol1").feature("t1").set("rtol", 1e-4); set("atolglobalmethod", "scaled"); set("atolglobal", 1e-4); set("atolmethod", new String[]{"comp1_T", "scaled"}); set("atol", new String[]{"comp1_T", "1e-3"})

parameters.name: rtol
parameters.description: Relative tolerance (study step or solver).

parameters.name: atolglobalmethod / atolglobal
parameters.description: Global absolute tolerance method (scaled | unscaled | factor) and value.

parameters.name: atolmethod / atol
parameters.description: Per-variable absolute tolerance method and value.

parameters.name: Tolerance factor / termination (stationary)
parameters.description: ntolfact on the Fully Coupled node; Stationary Solver rtol.

tools.notes: Scaled absolute tolerances are relative to the variable scale in Dependent Variables; unscaled ones are in physical units. Algebraic variables (DAEs) can be excluded from the error control with the 'Error estimation: exclude algebraic' option.

tools.name: Eigenvalue search settings (ARPACK / FEAST)
tools.description: Settings of the Eigenvalue Solver node (and the Eigenfrequency/Eigenvalue study steps) selecting the algorithm and search region: ARPACK (implicitly restarted Arnoldi with shift-invert, default) finds a given number of eigenvalues nearest a shift (or largest/smallest real/imaginary part), while FEAST (6.x) finds all eigenvalues inside a contour in the complex plane using contour integration and a stochastic estimate of their number, which is better for dense clusters and for parallel scaling. Related settings: eigenvalue transformation (eigenfrequency, effective mode index), scaling and the linearization point for nonlinear eigenvalue problems.
tools.usage: Study > Eigenfrequency > Desired number of eigenfrequencies / Search for eigenfrequencies around; Solver Configurations > Eigenvalue Solver > Eigenvalue method; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("e1").set("neigs", 6); set("shift", "100"); set("eigmethod", "manual"|"region"); set("eigsolv", "arpack"|"feast") (check names in the API solver reference)

parameters.name: neigs
parameters.description: Number of eigenvalues wanted (ARPACK).

parameters.name: shift
parameters.description: Value the search is centred on (eigenfrequency, eigenvalue or effective index).

parameters.name: eigwhich / Search method
parameters.description: Closest in absolute value | largest real | smallest real | largest imaginary ... (ARPACK).

parameters.name: Region (FEAST)
parameters.description: Rectangle/half-plane/contour in the complex plane; estimated number of eigenvalues.

parameters.name: Eigenvalue linearization / Real symmetric option
parameters.description: Speed-ups for undamped problems.

tools.notes: ARPACK may miss eigenvalues far from the shift or return spurious ones near a singular shift; asking for more modes than needed and checking with a second shift is good practice. Damped systems yield complex eigenfrequencies (imaginary part = decay rate; solid.Q_eig gives Q factor).

tools.name: MUMPS / PARDISO / SPOOLES / Dense Matrix Solver (Direct node)
tools.description: Solver choices of the Direct attribute node: MUMPS (default, multifrontal, supports distributed-memory clusters and out-of-core), PARDISO (Intel MKL, usually fastest on shared memory, out-of-core option, good for indefinite systems), SPOOLES (least memory, slowest, no longer recommended) and the Dense Matrix Solver for the boundary element method. All are robust LU factorizations whose memory grows quickly with 3D problem size; switch to an iterative solver above a few million DOFs. Pivoting thresholds, iterative refinement and the reuse of factorizations across load cases are set here.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Stationary/Time-Dependent Solver > Direct > Solver; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("s1").feature("d1").set("linsolver", "mumps"|"pardiso"|"spooles"|"dense"); set("ooc", "on"|"off"|"auto"); set("pivotperturb", 1e-8)

parameters.name: linsolver
parameters.description: mumps | pardiso | spooles | dense.

parameters.name: ooc
parameters.description: Out-of-core mode (writes factors to disk when memory is short).

parameters.name: pivotperturb / pivotstrategy
parameters.description: Pivot perturbation for PARDISO/MUMPS on ill-conditioned matrices.

parameters.name: iterrefine / errorchk
parameters.description: Iterative refinement steps and error check on the solution.

parameters.name: Reuse preordering / factorization
parameters.description: Speeds up repeated solves with identical sparsity or matrix.

tools.notes: MUMPS is required for cluster (distributed) direct solves; PARDISO is shared-memory only. The 'Direct' entry in the first solver chunk describes the node; memory estimates appear in the solver log ('Memory usage').

tools.name: GMRES / FGMRES / BiCGStab / Conjugate Gradients (Iterative node)
tools.description: Krylov solvers of the Iterative attribute node: GMRES (general, memory grows with the restart length), FGMRES (flexible - allows a preconditioner that changes between iterations such as another Krylov solver or multigrid with iterative smoothers; default for many physics), BiCGStab (short recurrence, low memory, less robust), Conjugate Gradients (symmetric positive definite systems only, cheapest) and TFQMR. Each is combined with a preconditioner (Multigrid, SOR, ILU, domain decomposition, Vanka, SCGS...) chosen by the physics defaults; the node sets the relative tolerance, maximum iterations, restart length and the error-estimate factor.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Stationary Solver > Iterative > Solver; API: model.sol("sol1").feature("s1").create("i1", "Iterative"); i1.set("linsolver", "gmres"|"fgmres"|"bicgstab"|"cg"|"tfqmr"); set("itrestart", 50); set("maxlinit", 1000); set("rhob", 400)

parameters.name: linsolver
parameters.description: gmres | fgmres | bicgstab | cg | tfqmr | precond (preconditioner only).

parameters.name: itrestart
parameters.description: Restart length for GMRES/FGMRES (default 50).

parameters.name: maxlinit
parameters.description: Maximum linear iterations (default 10000).

parameters.name: rhob
parameters.description: Factor in error estimate; larger accepts a less accurate linear solve per Newton step.

parameters.name: prefun (subnode)
parameters.description: Preconditioner created as a child: Multigrid, SOR, ILU, DomainDecomposition, Jacobi, Vanka, SCGS, AMS.

tools.notes: Iterative solvers need a good preconditioner far more than a good Krylov method; the physics-generated defaults (Suggested Iterative Solver nodes, right-click the solver) are the best starting point. Convergence plots appear under the solver log (Convergence Plot).

tools.name: SOR / Incomplete LU / Jacobi (preconditioner and smoother nodes)
tools.description: Simple preconditioners and multigrid smoothers: SOR (successive over-relaxation; forward/backward/symmetric variants, SOR Line, SOR Gauge for curl elements, SOR Vector) are the default smoothers in geometric/algebraic multigrid for most scalar and vector problems; Incomplete LU (ILU with drop tolerance and fill-in control, or ILUT) is a general stand-alone preconditioner for moderately sized nonsymmetric systems and a smoother for stiff problems; Jacobi (diagonal scaling) is the cheapest. Vanka and SCGS are the block smoothers for saddle-point systems (incompressible flow), and AMS is the auxiliary-space preconditioner for curl-curl problems.
tools.usage: Iterative > (right-click) Preconditioner / Multigrid > Presmoother > SOR; API: i1.create("so1", "SOR"); i1.create("ilu1", "ILU"); i1.create("jac1", "Jacobi"); mg1.feature("pr").create("so1", "SOR"); so1.set("iter", 2); so1.set("relax", 1.0)

parameters.name: iter
parameters.description: Number of iterations (sweeps) per application.

parameters.name: relax
parameters.description: Relaxation factor for SOR/Jacobi.

parameters.name: sorvector / sorline options
parameters.description: Variants for edge elements and anisotropic meshes.

parameters.name: droptol / fillratio (ILU)
parameters.description: Drop tolerance and fill-in limit controlling ILU accuracy versus memory.

tools.notes: Only one preconditioner (or multigrid) child is active per Iterative node; multigrid has separate Presmoother, Postsmoother and Coarse Solver subnodes where these appear again.

tools.name: Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) / Geometric Multigrid (GMG) settings
tools.description: Solver choices of the Multigrid attribute node: Geometric multigrid builds coarser meshes (by coarsening the mesh or lowering the element order, or using explicitly meshed Multigrid Level nodes) and is the most efficient for large 3D problems on meshable geometries, while Algebraic multigrid (classical AMG for scalar equations, smoothed aggregation SA-AMG for systems such as structural mechanics, and AMS for curl-curl) derives coarse levels from the matrix, needing no extra meshes and coping with complex geometry. Settings: number of levels, mesh coarsening factor, cycle type (V, W, F), smoothers and coarse solver (direct by default).
tools.usage: Iterative > Multigrid > Solver: Geometric multigrid | Algebraic multigrid | Smoothed aggregation AMG; API: i1.create("mg1", "Multigrid"); mg1.set("prefun", "gmg"|"amg"|"saamg"); set("mglevels", 5); set("mcasegen", "any"); set("mgcycle", "v"|"w"|"f"); set("rescaleaggregates", ...)

parameters.name: prefun
parameters.description: gmg | amg | saamg (and ams for magnetic fields).

parameters.name: mglevels / gmglevels
parameters.description: Number of multigrid levels.

parameters.name: mcasegen
parameters.description: Hierarchy generation: any | coarse (coarsen mesh) | lower order (reduce element order) | manual (Multigrid Level nodes).

parameters.name: mgcycle
parameters.description: v | w | f cycle.

parameters.name: Presmoother / Postsmoother / Coarse Solver subnodes
parameters.description: Smoother types and iterations, coarse-level direct solver.

tools.notes: GMG fails when the mesh cannot be coarsened (very thin geometry, imported meshes); AMG is the fallback. The 'Multigrid' entry in the first solver chunk describes the node itself.

tools.name: Domain Decomposition (preconditioner)
tools.description: Preconditioner node that splits the problem into overlapping (Schwarz: additive, multiplicative, hybrid, symmetric) or non-overlapping (Schur complement) subdomains solved separately by a direct or multigrid solver, with a coarse-level correction, so very large problems fit in memory (domain decomposition with 'recompute and clear' subdomain data) and scale on clusters. Used mainly for large acoustics/EM/structural problems where a direct solver runs out of memory and multigrid is not robust.
tools.usage: Iterative > Domain Decomposition; API: i1.create("dd1", "DomainDecomposition"); dd1.set("prefun", "ddmul"|"ddadd"|"ddhyb"|"ddsym"|"ddschurmul"|"ddschuradd"); set("ndom", 8); set("overlap", 1)

parameters.name: prefun
parameters.description: Schwarz variants (ddadd, ddmul, ddhyb, ddsym) or Schur complement (ddschuradd, ddschurmul).

parameters.name: ndom / overlap
parameters.description: Number of subdomains and overlap in element layers.

parameters.name: Domain solver / Coarse solver subnodes
parameters.description: Direct or Multigrid solvers per subdomain and for the coarse level.

parameters.name: Recompute and clear subdomain data
parameters.description: Trade CPU for memory.

tools.notes: Available in the core product (5.2+). Set the subdomain count so each subdomain fits comfortably in memory; more subdomains mean more iterations.

tools.name: Automatic Remeshing
tools.description: Attribute node of the Time-Dependent Solver used with Moving Mesh / Deformed Geometry: when the mesh quality (or a distortion measure) in the deforming domains drops below a threshold, the solver stops, generates a new mesh of the deformed configuration (with the original mesh settings), maps the solution onto it and continues, producing a sequence of Remeshed Solution nodes. Essential for large-motion FSI, free surfaces, corrosion/electrodeposition and actuator models; the mesh quality condition, remeshing frequency limit and the 'stop when remeshing fails' options are its settings.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Time-Dependent Solver > (right-click) Automatic Remeshing; or enable 'Automatic remeshing' in the Time Dependent study step (6.x); API: model.sol("sol1").feature("t1").create("ar1", "AutoRemesh"); ar1.set("condition", "quality"); ar1.set("minqual", 0.3)

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: Mesh quality | Distortion | Expression - what triggers remeshing.

parameters.name: minqual
parameters.description: Minimum acceptable element quality (0-1).

parameters.name: Consistent initialization / minimum time between remeshes
parameters.description: Restart behaviour after remeshing.

tools.notes: Each remesh interpolates the solution, introducing small errors; keep the trigger quality low enough that remeshing is rare. Results after remeshing span several solution datasets which COMSOL joins automatically in the default plots.

tools.name: Time Discrete Solver / Modal Solver / Time Explicit Solver
tools.description: Additional solver nodes generated for specific study types: the Time Discrete Solver steps through a time list with a user-supplied recursion (projection methods, the Time Discrete study), the Modal Solver integrates or sweeps the reduced modal equations for the Frequency Domain, Modal and Time Dependent, Modal studies (with modal damping settings and the option to output the reduced matrices), and the Time Explicit Solver drives the discontinuous Galerkin interfaces with explicit Runge-Kutta stepping and a CFL-based step size. They appear automatically in Solver Configurations for the corresponding study steps.
tools.usage: Study > Solver Configurations > Solution > Time Discrete Solver / Modal Solver / Time Explicit Solver; API: model.sol("sol1").create("td1", "TimeDiscrete"); model.sol("sol1").create("mo1", "Modal"); model.sol("sol1").create("te1", "TimeExplicit")

parameters.name: tlist
parameters.description: Time list (discrete or explicit solvers).

parameters.name: Modal: damping ratio / eigenpairs
parameters.description: Uniform or per-mode damping, source of eigenpairs (previous Eigenvalue Solver).

parameters.name: Time Explicit: CFL number / RK method
parameters.description: Step size factor and Runge-Kutta scheme (RK34, RK45...).

tools.notes: These nodes are normally created by 'Show Default Solver'; editing them by hand is rarely needed beyond the damping and step settings.

tools.name: Optimization Solver (SNOPT, MMA, IPOPT, Levenberg-Marquardt, Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA, Coordinate Search)
tools.description: Solver node generated by the Optimization / Parameter Estimation / Shape / Topology Optimization study steps that runs the optimisation loop around an inner Stationary/Time-Dependent/Frequency solver: gradient-based methods SNOPT (SQP, general constraints), MMA (method of moving asymptotes, topology optimisation), IPOPT (interior point) and Levenberg-Marquardt (least squares for parameter estimation) use adjoint or forward sensitivities and require differentiable models; derivative-free methods Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA and Coordinate Search work with any model including geometry parameters and mesh changes but need many more evaluations. Settings: optimality tolerance, maximum evaluations, control-variable and objective tables, constraint tolerance, and 'Keep solutions' for each iteration.
tools.usage: Study > Optimization step > Optimization solver: SNOPT | MMA | IPOPT | Levenberg-Marquardt | Nelder-Mead | BOBYQA | Coordinate search; Solver Configurations > Optimization Solver; API: model.study("std1").feature("opt").set("optmethod", "snopt"|"mma"|"ipopt"|"levenbergmarquardt"|"neldermead"|"bobyqa"|"coordsearch"); set("opttol", 1e-3); set("maxmodeleval", 1000); model.sol("sol1").create("o1", "Optimization")

parameters.name: optmethod
parameters.description: neldermead | bobyqa | cobyla | ego | ipopt | gcmma | mma | lm (COMSOL 6.4).

parameters.name: opttol / maxmodeleval / maxiter
parameters.description: Optimality tolerance and evaluation/iteration limits.

parameters.name: Objective / control variable tables
parameters.description: Global parameters or physics control variables with bounds and scales, objective expressions and constraints.

parameters.name: Gradient method
parameters.description: Adjoint | Forward | Numeric (finite difference) for gradient-based solvers.

parameters.name: Keep solutions / Probe output
parameters.description: Store every iteration or only the optimum; probe values per evaluation in a table.

tools.notes: Requires the Optimization Module. Parameter estimation with experimental data uses the Parameter Estimation study (Levenberg-Marquardt with Global Least-Squares Objective and experiment tables). The 'Optimization' study entry in the earlier chunk documents the study node at a high level. COMSOL 6.4 removed SNOPT: the study step setting is optmethod = neldermead | bobyqa | cobyla | ego | ipopt | gcmma | mma | lm (older optsolver/snopt calls are migrated to ipopt).

tools.name: Solver Log, Warnings and Convergence Plots
tools.description: Diagnostics attached to a solved sequence: the Log window (Study > Solver Configurations > Solution > (solver) > Log, and the Log tab of the Messages/Progress area) records assembly, memory, linear-solver and Newton/time-step statistics per iteration; Warning nodes appear under the solver features when the solver hit non-fatal issues (e.g. 'undefined value found', 'step reduction', 'reached maximum number of iterations'); and Convergence Plot windows show the error estimate per iteration/time step and the reciprocal step size, the first place to look when a run is slow or fails. In batch mode the same log goes to the -batchlog file.
tools.usage: Solver Configurations > Solution 1 > Stationary Solver 1 > Log tab; Warning nodes under solver features; Convergence Plot 1 window; Java: ModelUtil.showProgress(true) before model.sol(tag).runAll() prints the log to the console; batch: comsol batch ... -batchlog file.log

parameters.name: Keep log / Keep warnings
parameters.description: Solver settings that retain logs and warnings in the saved model.

parameters.name: Error estimate / Reciprocal of step size plots
parameters.description: Convergence plot contents for time-dependent solvers.

parameters.name: Solver statistics
parameters.description: Number of DOFs, memory, factorisation time, per-iteration residuals.

tools.notes: 'Failed to find a solution' messages point to the Newton damping, tolerances or the initial values; 'Singular matrix' to missing constraints (no ground, no pressure constraint, rigid-body modes). The Progress window's Cancel/Stop buttons stop the solve while keeping the last stored solution.
